nodes.label: ADR-0007 — Logical Status and Derived Views
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: Status folders couple lifecycle to physical structure and force unnecessary moves; status belongs to the object, views (approved/scheduled/completed/rejected/superseded) are derived by the Compiler so links and identities stay stable.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0007 — logical status and derived views

nodes.label: ADR-0008 — Human-Governed Evolution
nodes.author: Founder & CVO
nodes.rationale: Self-alteration of the canonical source erodes trust and traceability; in V1 Evolution only observes, analyzes and proposes with justification — 'AI proposes, human approves'. Future autonomy levels must be born as APs.

nodes.label: ADR-0009 — Taxonomy V1 Is Logical and Versioned
nodes.author: Founder & CVO
nodes.rationale: An initial taxonomy is needed to orient work, but treating it as permanent or as a directory mirror would block evolution; the future Ontology may confirm, redefine or replace its boundaries.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0009 — taxonomy v1 is logical and versioned

nodes.label: ADR-0010 — Adopt the Architectural Decision Filter
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: Weighted scoring was rejected because one quality could hide a critical flaw; automatic approval was rejected as conflicting with human governance. All criteria act as evidence-based gates; ADF pass grants eligibility, not Council approval.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0010 — adopt the architectural decision filter

nodes.label: ADR-0011 — Adopt the Implementation Handoff Protocol
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: Execution summaries do not preserve enough evidence for architectural review independent of the conversation or the CEA environment; informal summaries omit, full logs carry operational noise.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0011 — adopt the implementation handoff protocol

nodes.label: ADR-0012 — Prioritize System Overview in V1-M02
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: The project has distributed canonical decisions but no complete view able to orient a new AI without prior conversations; expanding the Ontology first risked low global comprehension, and turning README into the full view would mix onboarding with detailed architecture.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0012 — prioritize system overview in v1-m02

nodes.label: ADR-0013 — Model RFC as Specialized Knowledge
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: Promoting RFC to Core Type lacked ontological evidence; treating RFC as autonomous source conflicts with PMM-001; omitting it would leave pre-decision specification without explicit form. RFC is a specialized Knowledge object, not an independent Source of Truth.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0013 — model rfc as specialized knowledge

nodes.label: ACD-001 — Transição para Execução e Protocolos Fundamentais
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: Ends the initial architecture-definition phase; CEA enters incremental milestone execution. Establishes the mandatory milestone cycle and the rule that status belongs to the object, never to physical structure.
nodes.norm_label: acd-001 — transicao para execucao e protocolos fundamentais

nodes.label: AD-002 — Implementation Handoff Protocol Directive
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: Generic summaries do not let the CSA reconstruct real execution state without the conversation, CEA memory, or the dev environment; V1-M01 was retroactively returned from completed to pending_review.

nodes.label: AD-003 — Encerramento da V1-M01 e Início da V1-M02
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: Received as AD-002 (already taken by IHP directive); canonical ID advanced to AD-003 with source_designation preserved. Skills belong to the system, not the model/runtime of origin; Orchestrator stays as AP without implementation; no RFC/Skill/Agent/Orchestrator schema authorized at this checkpoint.
nodes.norm_label: ad-003 — encerramento da v1-m01 e inicio da v1-m02

nodes.label: AD-004 — Architectural Research Program
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: Institutes a permanent process to study and decompose external ideas before they become change proposals; popularity is not architectural evidence. Research informs or recommends but never approves architecture, never creates normative authority, never authorizes implementation.

nodes.label: AD-005 — Live Bootstrap Portability and Continuity Maintenance
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: A live bootstrap portability test showed the executor correctly refused authority from prompt text without a confirmed repo path; three gaps closed: GOV-001 made vendor/model-agnostic, README pointed to AGENT_START_HERE.md, Council decisions persisted as canonical ADs. Repository discovery is a responsibility external to the bootstrap — deferred to a future AP.
nodes.norm_label: ad-005 — live bootstrap portability and continuity maintenance

nodes.label: AD-006 — Temporary Dual-Role Execution Authorization (CVO)
nodes.author: Raphael Caveagna — Founder & CVO
nodes.rationale: Accepts reduced review independence temporarily in exchange for speed on low/medium-risk work already bounded by an accepted audit — and declares the cost instead of hiding it. Embedded CSA must seek gaps and disagree when merited; full agreement across reviews signals failure of the authorization. Excludes vision/philosophy changes, Ontology, G-17, CVO personal decisions (DH-1..6), Tier C.

nodes.label: GOV-002 — Operating Modes and Personal Low-Risk Governance Profile
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: Closes audit gaps G-A02 (modes undefined) and G-A14 (disproportionate governance for personal use). Contamination rule: a higher-mode requirement never enters a lower mode without recorded justification. Mode transition is a Council decision, never an implicit consequence of a feature. The profile reduces ceremony, not inherent risk (E73 §6: the bottleneck is writing overhead, not the Council).
nodes.norm_label: gov-002 — operating modes and personal low-risk governance profile

nodes.label: AIP-001 — Architectural Integrity Principle
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: No decision stands above the architecture: any CVO/CSA/CEA decision can be revised when technical evidence shows a superior architectural solution; long-lived systems lose coherence when decisions persist by hierarchy, habit or ego.

nodes.label: ACP-001 — Architectural Challenge Protocol
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: Operational autonomy without a duty to contest turns the executor into an amplifier of inconsistencies; on conflict the CEA must stop, explain, present alternatives, recommend the technically superior solution and await Council decision.

nodes.label: ADF-001 — Architectural Decision Filter
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: Prevents transient implementations, technologies or abstractions from being promoted to permanent components without evidence of lasting architectural value. No compensatory scoring: one criterion cannot hide another's failure; absence of evidence never equals approval.

nodes.label: Founder & Chief Vision Officer (CVO)
nodes.rationale: Defines objectives, priorities, philosophy and direction; sole authority on vision and product priority. Human judgment role — not delegable to a model.

nodes.label: Chief Systems Architect (CSA)
nodes.rationale: Stays above daily implementation; interprets the architectural source of truth without substituting it; approves or returns IHRs with architectural impact; may not approve its own work when also acting as executor of a slice.

nodes.label: Chief Execution Architect (CEA) / Executor
nodes.rationale: Operational autonomy within approved contracts; must trigger ACP on inconsistencies; does not approve its own result nor start the next stage on its own initiative. Exercisable by any model or person compatible with the bootstrap/Git/RETURN_SCHEMA contract.

nodes.label: Team Mode
nodes.rationale: Intentionally deferred; prerequisites: identity enforcement + Memory merge + concurrency (E70 §10).

nodes.label: Product Mode
nodes.rationale: Intentionally deferred; requires Team Mode plus tenancy/billing/abuse/conformance.

nodes.label: personal-low-risk Governance Profile
nodes.rationale: Proportional governance for local, reversible, externally inert actions in Personal Mode: IHR-lite, self-approval with solo_operator_exception, batch CSA review, Layer-1-only return, default budgets of ≤5 files and ≤2 commits. Git discipline, stopping rules, non-compensable blockers and PMM-001 are unchanged.

nodes.label: Project Memory
nodes.rationale: An architectural responsibility, not a directory: no important decision may exist exclusively inside a conversation; conversations generate ideas, Project Memory preserves them.

nodes.label: Authority Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: When sources conflict, the highest available authority prevails: Constitution (future) > Manifestos > Governance > Core Principles > ADRs > Architecture Documentation > Knowledge Objects > Roadmap > Milestones > Implementation.

nodes.label: Cognitive Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis of cognitive/governance flow: Idea → Knowledge Capture → Architecture Interview → RFC → Council Review → ADR → Planning → Orchestrator → Capability/Skill/Agent Selection → Execution → Validation → Documentation → Project Memory → Evolution. Does not yet define ontological types, contracts, automation or universal mandatory stages.

nodes.label: Architecture Interview (Skill candidate)
nodes.rationale: Approved as Skill candidate inspired by the 'Grill Me' pattern, without implementation.

nodes.label: Orchestrator (AP hypothesis)
nodes.rationale: Must remain an AP, not implemented; hypothesis includes coordinating the cognitive process, selecting Capabilities/Skills/Agents, evaluating RFC need, and deciding escalation and autonomy within governance.

nodes.label: RFC (specialized Knowledge object)
nodes.rationale: Describes a proposed change before implementation; derived from Project Memory and consistent with Manifestos, Principles, ADRs, APs; not an independent Source of Truth.

nodes.label: Taxonomy V1 (six logical domains)
nodes.rationale: Six logical domains — Foundation, Knowledge, Intelligence, Governance, Runtime, Evolution — versioned, revisable, independent of physical structure.

nodes.label: Governed Cognitive Loop
nodes.rationale: Experimental contractual pattern bounded by objective, planned context, authority, budget, useful unit, validation, progress, stopping, escalation, observability and proportional Project Memory recording. Not a Knowledge Type, Skill, Agent or mandatory Workflow.

nodes.label: Bounded Execution Loop
nodes.rationale: Operational policy applying the Governed Cognitive Loop pattern; its current limits are configurations, not ontological invariants.

nodes.label: Graphify (first registered research case)
nodes.rationale: First registered case of the Architectural Research Program — without adoption, integration or dependency.

nodes.label: Architectural Knowledge Evolution Map
nodes.rationale: Observation/Existing Knowledge → optional Research → optional AP → Decision → optional RFC/Plan → Execution → Validation/Operation → Evidence → Evolution. Experimental relational view, not a workflow, domain or Core Type; stages are optional and preserve many-to-many identities.

nodes.label: Adaptive Human Supervision (HotL/HitL)
nodes.rationale: Human-on-the-Loop applies to reversible, bounded, observable execution covered by authority; Human-in-the-Loop is mandatory for architecture, relevant canonical changes, irreversibility, high risk, material ambiguity, authority conflict, security exceptions, privileged access and relevant legal/financial/operational/privacy impacts.

nodes.label: Architectural Research Program (ARP profile)
nodes.rationale: Experimental Knowledge profile (knowledge_type: architectural_research_program, prefix ARP-NNNN, research_form: program|case|hypothesis) with lifecycle identified → scoped → authorized → active ↔ paused → concluded|terminated. Not a Core Type, domain, AP state or authority source.

nodes.label: Implementation Handoff Report (IHR)
nodes.rationale: Self-contained 12-section report (context, executed work, files, validation, plan vs execution, CEA decisions, documentation state, backlog, risks, Council questions, next action, evidence) persisted in Markdown next to its control point; experimental Knowledge specialization, not a Core Type.

nodes.label: Architectural Backlog
nodes.rationale: Every architectural idea is registered before implementation: Insight → Architectural Proposal → Council review → approval → adequate milestone → implementation → ADR when applicable → permanent artifact. In V1 the backlog review at each milestone end is manual and mandatory.

nodes.norm_label: adr-0003 — structural and human language convention

nodes.norm_label: adr-0005 — canonical and generated artifact policy

nodes.label: ARP, Knowledge Maturity and Governed Cognitive Loops Review (DRAFT)
nodes.author: Chief Execution Architect
nodes.norm_label: arp, knowledge maturity and governed cognitive loops review (draft)

nodes.label: Architectural Research (ARP)
nodes.author: Chief Execution Architect
nodes.rationale: Recommended as an experimental specialization of Knowledge, not a Core Type, to fill the gap between identifying a question/technology and proposing a change without polluting the AP backlog or prematurely growing the Ontology. Lifecycle: identified→scoped→authorized→active↔paused→concluded, with research_form: program|case|hypothesis as a single specialization rather than three types. Research informs AP/ADR/RFC but never creates authority automatically.

nodes.label: Knowledge Maturity Model (KMM)
nodes.author: Chief Execution Architect
nodes.rationale: Rejected as canonical workflow or type: the chain Knowledge→Research→AP→Decision→Execution→Operation→Evolution mixes knowledge artifacts, activities and system states with many-to-many relations. Recommended replacement: model knowledge evolution as a relational graph (Architectural Knowledge Evolution Map), not a mandatory pipeline.

nodes.label: Architectural Knowledge Evolution Map
nodes.author: Chief Execution Architect
nodes.rationale: Provisional view proposed instead of KMM: Observation/Knowledge → optional Research → optional AP → Decision → optional RFC/Plan → Execution → Validation/Operation → Evidence → Evolution, where arrows are permitted relations, not obligations; steps may be skipped depending on risk, novelty and evidence.

nodes.label: Governed Cognitive Loop
nodes.author: Chief Execution Architect
nodes.rationale: Treated as a contractual pattern / governance envelope over cycles, not a Core Type: explicit objective and authority, smallest useful unit per iteration, budgets (time, iterations, cost, effects), proportional validation, measurable progress, stop criteria defined before start, escalation on risk/ambiguity/authority, and Project Memory persistence without creating a parallel Source of Truth. Only becomes an object if persistent identity, composition, inspection or derived execution proves necessary.

nodes.label: Bounded Execution Loop
nodes.author: Chief Execution Architect
nodes.rationale: Classified as an operational policy and concrete example of the Governed Cognitive Loop pattern — not a Skill, not reducible to Strategy or Workflow. Its current concrete limits remain operational configuration and must not be elevated to ontological invariants.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-Loop
nodes.rationale: Adequate for irreversibility, architecture, high risk, ambiguity and authority conflicts — the human participates directly in approval or decision.

nodes.label: Human-on-the-Loop
nodes.rationale: AI operates within limits; the human supervises via checkpoints and gates — adequate for reversible, observable, bounded execution.

nodes.label: CVO–CSA–CEA Adaptive Supervision Model
nodes.author: Chief Execution Architect
nodes.rationale: The CVO–CSA–CEA governance model is an adaptive combination: human-on-the-loop for limited operational autonomy, human-in-the-loop for architectural, canonical, irreversible or high-risk decisions. No dedicated name or type should be created before testing this classification.

nodes.label: Architectural Evolution Backlog
nodes.rationale: Canonical living registry of architectural proposals: physical path never represents status (status is a logical YAML attribute; views are derived by the Compiler), review of all pending APs is mandatory at each milestone end, and no architectural idea may be implemented directly without first becoming an AP.

nodes.label: Architectural Proposal (AP)
nodes.rationale: In V1 each AP is a Knowledge object specialized by knowledge_type: architectural_proposal — not a Core Type; the Ontology may redefine this classification. States: proposed, approved, scheduled, completed, rejected, superseded. IDs follow AP-NNNN, immutable and never reused. Official flow: Insight → AP → Council review → approval → milestone → implementation → ADR when applicable → permanent artifact.

nodes.label: AP-0001 — Architectural Evolution Backlog
nodes.author: Raphael Caveagna — Founder & Chief Vision Officer

nodes.label: AP-0004 — Idea Lifecycle Engine
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: AI only proposes changes; every recommendation carries evidence; the canonical source is never modified without human approval.

nodes.label: AP-0006 — Formal System Ontology and Constitutional Metamodel
nodes.author: Raphael Caveagna — Founder & Chief Vision Officer
nodes.rationale: Define the fundamental language of the system before canonizing Capabilities, Agents, MCPs, Workflows or new types. Markdown, YAML, JSON and graphs are representations, not the Ontology. ADF (ASSESS-0001) result: remain_experimental — scheduled for V1-M02 without permanent promotion.
nodes.norm_label: ap-0006 — formal system ontology and constitutional metamodel

nodes.label: AP-0007 — Runtime-Agnostic Core and Adapter Contract
nodes.author: Raphael Caveagna — Founder & Chief Vision Officer
nodes.rationale: The core must never know or depend on Codex, Claude Code, GPT, Gemini, Cursor, Fable, n8n or any specific runtime; runtime-specific tools live exclusively behind adapters. Model agnosticism is a consequence; runtime agnosticism is the wider constraint.
nodes.norm_label: ap-0007 — runtime-agnostic core and adapter contract

nodes.label: AP-0008 — Project of Architectural Validation
nodes.author: Raphael Caveagna — Founder & Chief Vision Officer
nodes.rationale: Use the recurrent rebuild of a local Knowledge Inbox as a permanent conformance benchmark with eliminatory architectural gates: the final artifact is evidence; the architectural process is the real object under evaluation. Baseline is local, offline, no mandatory external AI.

nodes.label: AP-0009 — Architectural Decision Filter
nodes.author: Raphael Caveagna — Founder & Chief Vision Officer
nodes.rationale: Prevent transitory implementations, technologies or abstractions from being promoted to permanent components. ADF-001 establishes five evidence-based gates: simplicity, durability, fundamentality, generativity, agnosticism; outcomes are promotion-eligible, remain-experimental, or rejection.

nodes.label: AP-0010 — Implementation Handoff Protocol
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: Full architectural review must not depend on the conversation, the executor's memory or dev-environment access; IHP-001 defines triggers, twelve mandatory sections, Project Memory persistence, and forbids milestone closure without implementation, validation, documentation, backlog and review.

nodes.label: AP-0011 — AI Developer Experience
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: A new AI must be able to join, navigate, decide and contribute without conversational context or a specific runtime — reconstruct state without prior conversation, stay runtime agnostic, and never duplicate Project Memory, Governance or adapters.

nodes.label: AP-0012 — Orchestrator
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: Hypothetical central responsibility to understand context, select cognitive processes/Capabilities/Skills/Agents, decide when an RFC is required, coordinate execution, and decide autonomy vs escalation within governance contracts — form (component, Capability or artifact) intentionally undefined; hypotheses do not authorize implementation.

nodes.label: AP-0013 — Architecture Interview Skill Candidate
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: Reduce ambiguity before change specification via exhaustive, traceable architectural questioning (inspired by the 'Grill Me' pattern); approved only as a Skill candidate — implementation, contract and integration not authorized.

nodes.label: AP-0014 — Cognitive Pipeline
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: End-to-end conceptual view: Idea → Knowledge Capture → Architecture Interview → RFC → Council Review → ADR → Planning → Orchestrator → Capability/Skill/Agent Selection → Execution → Validation → Documentation → Project Memory → Evolution. Approved as conceptual direction only; the chain is a revisable hypothesis and does not authorize automation. Overlaps with AP-0005 (narrower evolution pipeline); Council to decide fusion/specialization later.

nodes.label: AP-0015 — Architecture Visualization Frontend
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: Every visualization must be derived from canonical sources; the interface must not allow silent divergence from Project Memory. Strategic registration only; frontend not authorized in V1-M02.

nodes.label: AP-0017 — NotebookLM Documentation Consumer
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: NotebookLM evaluated strictly as a disposable, derived consumer of official documentation: it never becomes a source of truth, inputs derive from versioned official documents, and removing the integration must cause no knowledge loss.

nodes.label: AP-0018 — Intent-Driven Cognitive Augmentation
nodes.author: Architecture Council
nodes.rationale: Intention-first experience: the user declares intent ('Tenho uma ideia') without knowing or selecting Agents, Skills, Capabilities or workflows; hiding operational complexity does not mean hiding decisions — selection, authority, risk and provenance stay explainable and auditable.

nodes.rationale: Chosen over personal-organization, education, market-research and customer-service candidates because it is familiar, non-regulated at its core, and naturally supports authority/approval and evidence questions with only moderate domain assumptions.

nodes.label: Fidelity Option B: Structured Interactive Prototype
nodes.rationale: Option A (low-fidelity flows) cannot test cross-state interaction, approval consequences or recovery; Option C (high-fidelity visual) answers questions outside current uncertainty and risks polish masking comprehension defects. Option B is the smallest option covering PQ-01..20 at the right conceptual level, with explicit simulation annotation to avoid being mistaken for real behavior.
nodes.norm_label: fidelity option b: structured interactive prototype

nodes.label: Journeys J1..J6 (First use, Discovery, Plan review, Execution, Evidence review, Return)
nodes.norm_label: journeys j1..j6 (first use, discovery, plan review, execution, evidence review, return)

nodes.label: Separation of Duties
nodes.rationale: Proposal does not self-authorize; executor does not accept its own outcome; evidence producer cannot certify; CSA recommends but does not decide; Council approval cannot manufacture missing evidence. Execution capability != decision authority; visibility != permission.

nodes.label: Approval Contract (scoped authorization record)
nodes.rationale: Every approval records decision, actor, rationale, scope/version, inputs, effects, risks, authority, reversibility, expiry and alternatives. A bare 'Continuar?' prompt is an anti-pattern; approval is scoped authorization, not certification.

nodes.label: Non-compensable Blockers B-01..B-09
nodes.rationale: Desired quality (polish, efficiency) can never compensate a blocker such as execution without authority, misleading approval effect, unrecoverable failure, critical keyboard/AT barrier or invented progress. No aggregate score is allowed.

nodes.label: Limited Hybrid IA Baseline
nodes.rationale: Pure object-centered IA leaks ontology; pure lifecycle implies false linearity; pure task-centered hides lineage; pure project-centered hides pending cross-object action. A limited hybrid (persistent project context + task entry + contextual links + search/recent/pending) is most proportional.

nodes.label: Ontology Leakage Review
nodes.rationale: Repository folders, Knowledge Types, internal IDs (ARP/IHR), governance role names and graph-mirrored ontology must not become the product IA or copy; Stage 2 must test terminology and mental models rather than encode internal taxonomy in layout. Review concluded no ontology change is required.

nodes.label: Assistance Levels A0..A3
nodes.rationale: A3 (direct help) completes the learning opportunity but marks the task completed_with_help; required assistance is itself evidence and must be recorded, never hidden.

nodes.label: G-17 Explicit Council Authorization Artifact
nodes.rationale: A signed explicit authorization artifact with dates, scope, ceilings and authority is absolute and never waivable; document approval alone can never substitute it. Even after all other gates close, a new explicit Council decision is required.

nodes.label: No-Recording Baseline
nodes.rationale: No audio, video or screen recording: minimum collection and infrastructure; moderator plus independent note taker with structured fields substitute. Any recording exception reopens the proposal and privacy review.

nodes.label: Retention Schedule (30/90/180 days)
nodes.rationale: Mapping/contact/payment deleted within 30 days after reconciliation; pseudonymized raw notes deleted 90 days after Council decision, absolute maximum 180 days from collection; de-identified findings follow the ARP evidence lifecycle; backups must not silently restore deleted data.

nodes.label: Paraphrase-Only Quote Policy
nodes.rationale: Direct/verbatim quotes excluded because no recording is used, exact wording is difficult to verify, and re-identification value exceeds current decision need; a short quote would require a separate consent opt-in and reopened privacy approval.

nodes.label: Finding F-01: Internal Vocabulary Leakage ('CEA simulado') on Authorization Surface
nodes.rationale: Material, not blocker: the labeled Executor field keeps authority semantics understandable even with an opaque value. Correcting immediately would invalidate the G-03 freeze hash candidates and consume the single material correction cycle without blocker-level need; fix deferred to a future E29/E30 v1.1 before any participant evaluation.
nodes.norm_label: finding f-01: internal vocabulary leakage ('cea simulado') on authorization surface

nodes.label: Domain Extraction Feasibility Experiment (experiments/clite-domain-extraction-feasibility)
nodes.rationale: Dependency inversion: the experimental ScenarioFixture contract is injected by parameter, removing the fixture-as-module-import and UI-in-AppState couplings; 74/74 tests pass on two distinct fixtures compiled without the DOM lib, proving browser and scenario independence. Does not prove concurrency, multi-user or product validity.

nodes.label: Stale Context Split Decision (domain vs presentation)
nodes.rationale: Stale context (stale_view guard + PROJECT_RESUMED/refresh) is domain because it implements Derived Status != Canonical Decision and is testable without a browser; view navigation (ViewId, idle/busy/error) is presentation and stays out of the extracted domain.
nodes.norm_label: stale context split decision (domain vs presentation)

nodes.label: Canonical Project Memory Adapter Feasibility Experiment (experiments/clite-memory-adapter-feasibility)
nodes.norm_label: canonical project memory adapter feasibility experiment (experiments/clite-memory-adapter-feasibility)

nodes.label: Event History Option D (hybrid: checkpoints in Memory + separate audit artifact)
nodes.rationale: Full event log in Memory rejected: unreadable for humans, unbounded growth, mixes audit with Memory, hurts merge and privacy. Option D keeps accepted markers plus provenance refs in the Memory document while the complete log lives in a separate optional audit artifact, honoring Audit trail != Memory (E58).
nodes.norm_label: event history option d (hybrid: checkpoints in memory + separate audit artifact)

nodes.label: Stimulus Change: Executable Vertical Slice Replaces Markdown Prototype
nodes.rationale: The Stage 3 executable slice corrected material finding F-01, implements real state that the Markdown medium could not (F-03/F-04/F-06), and already has structural accessibility verification (E49); using it as the study stimulus partially invalidates the G-04 renderer premise and reduces the moderation notes needed for F-02/F-04.
nodes.norm_label: stimulus change: executable vertical slice replaces markdown prototype

nodes.label: Session Method Option D (task-based + post-action probes + retrospective)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over guided walkthrough (moderator narrates, comprehension untested), pure task sessions (weak for reasoning) and think-aloud (heavy for cohort B, conflicts with AT): Option D captures action AND reasoning with controllable moderator bias, since probes come only after the action and verbalization is invited, never required.
nodes.norm_label: session method option d (task-based + post-action probes + retrospective)

nodes.label: Cohort A/B Participant Strategy (4-6 participants, 2A+2B minimum)
nodes.rationale: Below 4 participants recurrence across cohorts cannot be observed; 6 keeps E34 ceilings respected from below while sufficient for qualitative signal. Cohort B (non-technical creators) is where ontology leakage would surface. Order alternates A/B so moderation learning does not favor one cohort.
nodes.norm_label: cohort a/b participant strategy (4-6 participants, 2a+2b minimum)

nodes.label: Proportional Separation-of-Duties for Minimal Study (2 operators + CSA + Council)
nodes.rationale: Moderator and note taker must be different people in a session because the independent record is the only evidence source without recording; the reviewer cannot be only the prototype author; Council decision authority is never accumulable with operations. Low-risk accumulations are registered as exceptions, never presented as independent review.
nodes.norm_label: proportional separation-of-duties for minimal study (2 operators + csa + council)

nodes.label: Evaluation Roles and Accountability Model (14 roles)
nodes.norm_label: evaluation roles and accountability model (14 roles)

nodes.label: Graph Deferral Decision
nodes.rationale: Graph is deferred entirely: it would add visual/interaction/tool questions without answering a core uncertainty. A simple accessible relation/history list in SF-07/08 covers artifact-evidence-decision lineage; HP-09 failure or later impact-analysis needs can reopen the decision.

nodes.label: Search Exclusion Decision
nodes.rationale: Interactive search excluded from the first prototype because none of PQ-01..20 requires it to complete the core cycle; contextual links, recent changes and pending actions suffice. Reopen only if return/findability tasks cannot be evaluated without it.

nodes.label: In-Person Controlled-Device Session Baseline
nodes.rationale: Recommended because the selected renderer candidate is local and version fidelity/reset are central; remote controlled-device is backup only after conferencing/remote-control/privacy/accessibility gates; participant-device sessions need a separately validated delivery package.
